title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Chewy chocolate chip cookies with golden, crisp edges and soft centers, made with brown sugar, vanilla and plenty of semisweet chips.
scaleNote: A large baking sheet holds about 12 cookies, so more cookies just means more rounds. The bake time per sheet stays the same.

image.alt: Illustration of chocolate chip cookies on a plate

ingredients.note: it should dent easily when pressed but still hold its shape

steps.text: Heat the oven to {temp 375F oven} with a rack in the middle. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper. In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, baking soda and salt.
In a large bowl, beat the butter, brown sugar and granulated sugar with an electric mixer on medium speed until lighter in color and fluffy, {time 2-3 min}.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed. The mixture should look smooth, not curdled.
Add the flour mixture and mix on low speed just until no streaks of flour remain. Stir in the chocolate chips with a spatula.
Scoop the dough into balls of about {qty 3 tbsp fixed} each and set them on the lined sheets with a {len 2 in} gap between them, about 12 per sheet.
Bake one sheet at a time until the edges are golden but the centers still look pale and a little soft, {time 10-12 min}. The centers firm up as the cookies cool.
Let the cookies cool on the sheet for {time 5 min}, then move them to a wire rack. Bake the remaining dough on a cool sheet; a hot sheet makes the cookies spread too much.

notes: For thicker cookies with a deeper caramel flavor, cover and chill the scooped dough for at least {time 1 hr notimer} or up to 3 days. Bake straight from the fridge, adding {time 1-2 min notimer}.
To freeze, set scooped dough balls on a tray until firm, then keep them in a freezer bag for up to 3 months. Bake from frozen, adding {time 2-3 min notimer}.
If the butter is greasy or starting to melt, the cookies will spread thin. Chill the dough for {time 30 min notimer} before scooping.
Store cooled cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days.
